evidence.note: Title claims a speed change: returns take three days instead of eleven.
Diagram is a plain three-box flow (Return request -> Warehouse -> Refund) with no durations or before/after comparison, so it does not show three vs eleven days.
A numbered three-item step list on the left restates the same flow in text alongside the diagram.
A column of three quote tiles (Customer, Warehouse lead, Finance) sits to the right of the diagram.
At the smaller size the title, step list, diagram, three tiles and caption 'Median days, January to March, all regions' all compete in a narrow viewport.
Step 0 shows an empty diagram panel next to the step list and caption.

rationale: The title's message (3 days vs 11) is not carried by the visual, which shows only a process flow with no timing, so the title and visual point different ways. The slide stacks a title, numbered step list, diagram, a column of quote tiles and a caption, matching the fail anchor's crammed layout. A viewer would need to read everything to connect the flow to the speed claim.
